description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the modules-work battery (#1994, mw-12).  Probe vs perl 5.40.3: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/hashctor1.pl (rows 1-3 announced as drops; rows 4-6 compile).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.  The inner `{ map {...} @l }` / `{ g(@l) }` is being read as a BLOCK, not as an anonymous hash, inside the deref braces -- perl's own heuristic for `{` at the start of a deref block is "looks like an anon hash" when the first thing is a `map`/word followed by `=>`/`,` ... but here perl sees `%{ BLOCK }` whose block's single statement is `{ map ... }` and treats THAT as an anon hash constructor because a bare block would not yield a hash ref -- probe perl's answers for `%{{ map { ($_, 1) } @l }}`, `%{{ %h, extra => 1 }}`, `%{{ @pairs }}`, `%{{ f() }}`, `@{{ a => [1] }}{a}`.  PExpr already has `_block_is_hash_constructor()` for the map/grep block-vs-hash question (CLAUDE.md TODO section, s62): route the deref-block's inner brace through the SAME classifier (rule 11) rather than a new guess.  The refusal is loud, so this is a gap and not a silent wrong.  BAR: `Pl/` => corpus-diff (list the corpus sites with `%{{`; they are drops today -- check the drop census rows that leave BY EDIT), gate-SET scan both populations (a refusal stops firing), gen bump + artifacts, guard rows in an existing anon-hash/deref Pl/t file.


=== DONE (s500a, Opus, 2026-09-30) ===
PERL'S RULE (probed 5.40.3, scratch/s500a/probes/hashctor2.pl, 22 rows + Deparse): a brace group that OPENS a deref block -- `%{{ … }}`, `%{ { … } }`, `@{{ … }}{…}`, `${{ … }}{…}` -- is ALWAYS an anonymous hash, whatever it holds (a map, a call, `%h`, `@pairs`, a literal list, `lc("A"), 1`).  The block-shaped spellings are compile-time syntax errors in perl (`%{ { my $x = 1; (a => $x) } }`, `%{ {} }`, `%{{}}`), so no valid program reads a block there.
FIX: Pl::PExpr::_block_is_hash_constructor gains a position argument; 'deref' answers 1 (the map/grep/lone-term rule is unchanged).  `_deref_inner_brace` recognises PPI's shape (the deref Block's only statement is a Statement::Compound holding only a bare Structure::Block) and the lone-Block arm routes it through the classifier into the existing hash_init lowering.  PPI already made `%{{ a => 1 }}` a Constructor; the WORD-first contents were the bare-block guesses.
PROBES: hashctor2.pl 22/22 = perl (13 were drops on the base); breaking cases hashctor3.pl: map/grep/sort/do/eval/anon-sub/if bodies holding a bare block, `{ g(@l) }` as a my-init, `%{{ g() }}` as a whole-hash copy -- all unchanged.  Two PRE-EXISTING divergences found and NOT this task's: `[ { g(@l) } ]` builds 4 elements where perl builds ONE anon hash (term position, same classifier, filed #2540); `sort { { $a <=> $b } }` (perl reads a hash; recorded in #2540).
GUARDS: Pl/t/braced-bareword-deref-01.t rows 16-20 (all fail on base).  Everyday modules/Text-Wrap-ParseWords-Abbrev is `same`.
CORPUS: the corpus's `%{{…}}` sites (tr.t:1047/1088) are Constructor-shaped already -- no emission change; gate-SET scan (both populations, 638 files) IDENTICAL.
subject: LOUD GAP (everyday idiom): `%{{ LIST }}` -- a hash DEREF of an anonymous hash constructor whose contents are a `map` or a call -- is a whole-statement refusal: the classic uniq `my @u = keys %{{ map { $_ => 1 } @l }};` dies "PCL: statement not supported ... Handle single node of unknown type"; the spaced spelling `%{ { map ... } }` and `%{{ g(@l) }}` likewise; `%{ +{ ... } }`, `%{{ a => 1, b => 2 }}` (a literal pair list) and `@{[ map ... ]}` compile
